create.name: Valerie Brown
create.bio:
Valerie Brown is a Dharma teacher who draws on two contemplative paths at once: the mindfulness practice of Thich Nhat Hanh's Plum Village community, which she began in 1995 and in which she was ordained as a teacher in 2018, and the silent worship and discernment of the Quakers. Before teaching she spent around twenty years as a lawyer and lobbyist, and she often describes the Camino de Santiago as the walk that turned her towards contemplative life. She later trained as a facilitator with Parker Palmer's Center for Courage & Renewal and in eco-Dharma teaching.

She leads silent nature retreats, Circle of Trust retreats on life transitions and small-group pilgrimages to the Camino, and gives Dharma talks for sanghas, Upaya Zen Center, New York Insight and Quaker gatherings, many of them posted on her YouTube channel. Her books include Hope Leans Forward, on simplicity and steadiness in hard times; Healing Our Way Home, a conversation between three Black women teachers in the Plum Village tradition, written with Marisela B. Gomez and Kaira Jewel Lingo; and The Mindful School Leader, with Kirsten Olson. Much of her writing and teaching centres on belonging, social justice and contemplative practice for people of colour. She lives in New Hope, Pennsylvania, and also works as a leadership coach.

books.title: Hope Leans Forward: Braving Your Way toward Simplicity, Awakening, and Peace
books.author: Valerie Brown
books.description: A memoir-led book in which Valerie Brown pairs stories from her own life with contemplative practices from the Buddhist and Quaker traditions. It looks at living more simply and keeping hope alive through uncertain times, with reflections and exercises at the end of each chapter.

books.title: Healing Our Way Home: Black Buddhist Teachings on Ancestors, Joy, and Liberation
books.author: Kaira Jewel Lingo, Valerie Brown, Marisela B. Gomez
books.description: Three Black women who teach in the Plum Village tradition talk frankly about family, ancestors, relationships, race and joy. Their conversations are interspersed with short reflective practices for readers to try.

books.title: The Mindful School Leader: Practices to Transform Your Leadership and School
books.author: Valerie Brown, Kirsten Olson
books.description: Written with Kirsten Olson for head teachers and school administrators, this book sets out simple mindfulness practices for a demanding job. It draws on interviews with educators who have brought the practice into their schools.

courses.title: Pilgrimage to Silence: A Nature Based Retreat for Rest & Renewal
courses.description: A five-night silent retreat at Hollyhock on Cortes Island that treats the stay itself as a pilgrimage. Days combine Plum Village-style sitting and walking meditation, mindful meals and time outdoors with Quaker-inspired reflection and small-group sharing.
courses.price: All-inclusive package (tuition, lodging and meals); price depends on accommodation and is shown at registration

courses.title: Navigating Life Transitions: A Courage & Renewal® Retreat
courses.description: A Circle of Trust retreat at Hollyhock, based on Parker Palmer's Courage & Renewal approach, for people at a turning point in work, relationships or later life. It uses poetry, silence, movement and a form of the Quaker clearness committee to help each person hear their own inner guidance.
courses.price: All-inclusive package (tuition, lodging and meals); price depends on accommodation and is shown at registration

courses.title: Healing Our Way Home: A Retreat for Women of Color
courses.description: A weekend at the Garrison Institute in New York for women of colour, led with her co-authors Marisela Gomez and Kaira Jewel Lingo. It draws on their two books, with Dharma talks, sitting and moving meditation, chanting, writing and small-group sharing; booking is through the Garrison Institute.

courses.title: Pilgrimage: the Art of Sacred Travel
courses.description: Valerie's Walk in Beauty pilgrimages are small-group walks on the Camino de Santiago in Spain, run roughly every other year. Walkers meet online in the months before setting out, then travel at an unhurried pace with reflection, silence and shared meals along the way.

free_resources.title: Cultivating Metta For Everyone
free_resources.description: A free guided loving-kindness meditation of about fourteen minutes on Insight Timer. Valerie leads listeners through offering goodwill to themselves and then outwards to other people.
